question: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India gave the status of state to Goa?
solution:
The correct answer is __56th Amendment__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **56th Amendment Act,** 1987 of the Indian Constitution conferred Statehood on Goa and forms a new Union Territory of Daman and Diu.
 
• Goa thus became the 25th State of the Indian Republic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 52nd Amendment:

 
 
• 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 of the Indian Constitution provided provisions related to anti-defection in India.
 
• In this amendment, articles 101, 102, 190 and 191 were changed.
 
• It laid down the process by which legislators may be disqualified on grounds of defection and inserted the tenth schedule.
 
 

 
• 59th Amendment:

 
 
• 59th Amendment Act, 1988 of the Indian Constitution empowered the Central Government to impose an Emergency in Punjab when deemed necessary.
 
• Under the amendment, the President's rule can be extended up to three years.
 
 
 
• **48th amendment Act, 1984:**
 
 
• Facilitated the extension of the President's rule in Punjab beyond one year without meeting the two special conditions for such extension.
